hints: Look closely at the two groups circled in each diagram. One should come from a carboxyl group (-COOH) and the other from an amino group (-NH2).
Remember condensation to make a peptide bond always removes OH from the C=O end and H from the N-H end to make H2O, leaving C joined directly to N.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two reacting groups**

Each amino acid has an amino end (-NH2) on the left and a carboxyl end (-COOH) on the right. To join two amino acids, the -COOH of one must react with the -NH2 of the next.

Look for OH leaving one molecule and H leaving the other:
$$-COOH + H_2N- \rightarrow -CO-NH- + H_2O$$

**Check what makes water**

A peptide bond is a condensation reaction. The OH comes from the carboxyl group (C-OH) and the H comes from the amino group (N-H). Together they form $H_2O$.

**Match to the diagrams**

Only diagram A circles OH from the left C=O end and H from the right N-H end. That is exactly the correct pair to release water and leave a C-N peptide bond. Great spotting!

options.A: Correct. OH is taken from the carboxyl group of the left amino acid and H is taken from the amino group of the right amino acid, forming H2O and a C-N peptide bond.
options.B: False. Both circled groups are OH from two carboxyl ends, so this would be carboxyl to carboxyl, not carboxyl to amino.
options.C: False. It circles O from C=O and H atoms from N, but water must use OH from the carboxyl, not the double-bonded O.
options.D: False. It circles O and OH from two carboxyl ends, so no amino group H is involved and no C-N peptide bond can form.
